answer.diagnosis: Likely shortcut: overall background brightness. Most trained layer-1 units are size detectors with clear centre and annulus structure. Small-blob units (0,3,5,8,14,15,18,20,23,24,25,28,31) have a negative annulus and a positive centre. Large-blob units (1,6,9,10,11,12,16,27,30) have a positive annulus. Units 2,4,7,13,17,21,22,26,29 look untrained. On top of that structure, the small-blob units carry a large uniform positive offset (about +20 to +43 integer units) on every far-background pixel: the corners and border bands, which no blob ever covers. Large-blob units carry small or negative offsets there. Unit 19 is a pure brightness detector: uniform positive weights of about 50 over the whole image, slightly lower at the centre. The background offsets are far larger than these units' bias changes would be if the background were unrelated to the label. That pattern means background-pixel intensity was correlated with the class during training, so the net reads background brightness as evidence of blob size. Bright background pushes toward the small-blob units. Fix: in the 320-pixel border region (rows 0-3, rows 20-23, and columns 0-3 and 20-23 of rows 4-19), subtract each affected unit's uniform background offset. Do the same over the whole grid of brightness unit 19. Fold the removed constant into each bias at an assumed background level of about 0.2, so the units keep their operating point. The centre and annulus size detectors are left unchanged. Caveat: the bias compensation depends on that assumed background level.
